# code flow

> A tiny workflow engine in Python. A workflow is a class with one @flow
> body of ordinary Python; the @step methods it calls are journaled, so a
> resumed run replays the body and completed steps return instantly.
> This file is a complete, accurate reference for LLMs writing flows.

## Anatomy

Drop a `.py` file anywhere under `workflows/` (subfolders scanned
recursively; each folder on the path becomes a tag; files/folders starting
with `_` are ignored — shared code goes in `workflows/_lib/`, imported as
`from _lib.helpers import x`). The folder is re-scanned per request, so
edits apply without a restart.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Literal
from engine import Workflow, flow, step, parallel_map

@dataclass                                # typed inputs (optional but preferred)
class DeployInputs:
    service: Literal["payments", "orders"] = "payments"   # -> select
    replicas: int = field(default=3, metadata={"min": 1, "max": 20})
    canary: bool = True
    # str->string  int->integer  float->number  bool->boolean
    # Literal/Enum->select  list/dict/other->json  Optional[X]->X not required
    # no default => required; extras via field(metadata={min,max,help,label,
    # options,required,type}) or Annotated[int, {"min": 1}]

class DeployFlow(Workflow):
    description = "Shown in the UI"
    tags = ["devops"]                     # UI grouping/filtering
    inputs = DeployInputs                 # the CLASS, not an instance.
                                          # a plain dict = untyped defaults
    dashboard = False                     # True => Dashboards tab
    webhook = False                       # True => POST /api/hooks/DeployFlow
    # webhook_token = "secret"            # optional per-flow webhook auth

    @flow                                 # EXACTLY ONE per class
    def main(self, ctx):                  # ctx = validated inputs + ctx["env"]
        art = self.build(ctx["service"])          # journaled step call
        hosts = self.discover_hosts(ctx["service"])
        if ctx["canary"]:                          # real if
            self.push(art, hosts[0])
        for h in hosts[1:]:                        # real for
            self.push(art, h)
        parallel_map(lambda h: self.push(art, h), hosts, workers=4)
        try:                                       # real try/except
            self.smoke_test()
        except Exception:
            self.rollback(); raise
        return {"deployed": True}                  # dict return -> outputs

    @step(retry=3, retry_delay=2, retry_backoff=2,
          retry_on=(ConnectionError, TimeoutError),
          timeout=30, continue_on_error=False, name="Push")
    def push(self, artifact: str, host: str) -> str:
        self.log(f"pushed {artifact} to {host}")
        return host
```

## Rules that matter

1. Exactly one `@flow` method; signature `(self, ctx)`. Without it the class
   is not discovered.
2. Steps take ordinary args and return ordinary values. Nothing is merged
   into a shared context — use variables.
3. **The body must be pure and deterministic.** On resume it re-executes
   from the top (completed steps return from the journal). So:
   - real work and side effects go inside `@step` methods;
   - no `datetime.now()`, `random`, `uuid`, file writes or HTTP in the body;
   - `self.sleep(sec)` instead of `time.sleep` (journaled + cancellable).
4. Retries/timeouts/journaling are **per call**: a step called in a loop
   gets independent attempts and one journal entry per iteration, so a
   failed loop resumes at the failed item.
5. `next=`, `condition=`, `loop=`, `parallel=`, `resumable=`, `@start`,
   `@wait` and `inputs_schema` were REMOVED. Use Python / a dataclass.
6. `inputs` is a dataclass TYPE or a plain dict — never an instance. The
   body always gets a plain dict `ctx`, so `ctx["service"]`, not `ctx.service`.

## @step parameters

name · retry · retry_delay · retry_backoff · retry_on · continue_on_error
(returns None instead of raising after all attempts) · timeout (raises
StepTimeoutError; the attempt is abandoned, not killed — keep such steps
duplicate-safe).

## Workflow API (inside body or steps)

self.log(msg) · self.log_json(obj, title="") · self.log_table(rows, title="")
self.log_image(path|bytes|data-URI|matplotlib fig, title="", format="png")
self.outputs({...})            # merge into run outputs
self.widget(type, **props)     # dashboards
self.sleep(seconds)            # journaled, cancellable
self.env                       # selected environment dict (real values)
self.call_workflow("Other", inputs={...}, env=None)
    # child run with its own report (↳ in history); returns its outputs;
    # raises if it fails; inherits env unless env="name"; cycles detected
parallel_map(self.step_method, items, workers=4)   # module-level import

## Environments & secrets

`environments/*.json` — file name = env name, chosen per run. Values may
reference OS env vars: `"api_token": "${MY_TOKEN}"` (resolved at load;
missing var -> warning). ${}-resolved values and secret-named keys
(*token*, *secret*, *password*, *api_key*, *credential*, *private*) are
masked in UI/reports but NOT in `self.log` lines — never log secrets.
Common flag: `"dry_run": true` + `if not self.env.get("dry_run"):`.

## Dashboards

`dashboard = True`; build widgets in steps with `self.widget(...)`. Refresh
re-runs the flow transiently (no history entry). Input widgets come from
the inputs dataclass (or inferred from dict defaults). Types: metric(value) ·
stat(value, delta) · status(value, status=ok|warn|err|neutral) ·
progress(value, max) · table(rows, format=[...]) · chart(chart=bar|line|
area|pie, data=dict|list) · list(items) · alert(text, level=info|warn|error)
· text · json(value) · html · link(url) · section(title). size: "" | "wide"
| "full". Table formatting: `format=[{"col":"status","map":{"paid":"ok"}},
{"col":"amount","gt":300,"style":"err"}]`; ops eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/contains;
styles ok|warn|err|info|muted; first match wins.

## Failure & history

A step fails by RAISING; the run stops unless `continue_on_error=True`
(which returns None to the caller). History actions: ↺ restart (fresh run,
same inputs/env) · ⏭ resume (replays the body; completed steps show as
"carried over") · cancel (cooperative: takes effect at the next step
boundary, or within ~0.25s inside a step that has `timeout=`).
Tolerant loops: catch inside the step and return a marker
(`{"item": x, "ok": False, "error": ...}`) instead of raising.

## Scheduler & webhooks

Schedules: `{"flow", "type": "interval"|"daily", "every_minutes" |
"time"+"days"(0=Mon..6=Sun), "inputs", "env", "enabled"}`; server-local
time; an overlap guard skips a fire while the previous run is RUNNING.
Webhook: `webhook = True`, then `POST /api/hooks/<Flow>` with the JSON body
as inputs (`?env=`, token via `X-Webhook-Token` or `?token=`; per-flow
`webhook_token` or global `CODEFLOW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN`).

## REST API (full doc: docs/API.md)

GET  /api/flows                     POST /api/run/<flow> {"inputs","env"}
GET  /api/runs                      GET  /api/runs/<id>
POST /api/runs/<id>/cancel          POST /api/runs/<id>/restart
POST /api/runs/<id>/resume          DELETE /api/runs/<id> | /api/runs
POST /api/runs/bulk-delete          GET  /api/environments
POST /api/dashboards/<flow>/render  GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/schedules...
POST /api/hooks/<flow>              GET  /reports/<id>   (HTML report)
Statuses: RUNNING SUCCESS FAILED CANCELLED INTERRUPTED.
Typed-input failures: 422 `{"detail":{"message","errors":{field:msg}}}`.

## Linting (run after generating a flow)

`python -m engine.lint workflows` (exit 1 on errors; `--strict` fails on
warnings; `--json`). Rules: CF001 duplicate step name · CF002 no @flow ·
CF003 multiple @flow · CF004 removed graph argument (next/condition/loop/
parallel/resumable) · CF005 @start/@wait removed · CF020 inputs_schema
removed · CF021 inputs is a class but not a @dataclass · CF010 retry= without
timeout= · CF011 swallowed exception in a step · CF012 possible secret in a
log line · CF013 call at import time · CF014 missing description · CF030
non-determinism in a body · CF031 side effect in a body.

## Config (env vars / .codeflow.env)

CODEFLOW_WORKFLOWS_DIR · CODEFLOW_ENVIRONMENTS_DIR · CODEFLOW_HISTORY_DIR ·
CODEFLOW_HISTORY_LIMIT (500) · CODEFLOW_HOST/PORT (127.0.0.1:8000) ·
CODEFLOW_WEBHOOK_TOKEN · CODEFLOW_SCHEDULES_FILE. No authentication — keep
on localhost/Tailscale. requests, PyYAML, dirtyjson preinstalled.

## Pitfalls (verified)

- Two steps with the same name=: the second silently wins (CF001).
- Side effects or `now()`/`random` in the body re-run on resume (CF030/031).
- Step results must be JSON-serializable to restore exactly on resume.
- A timed-out step call is abandoned, not killed — make it duplicate-safe.
- `parallel_map` uses threads: I/O yes, CPU no.
- Parent `retry=` around `call_workflow` re-runs the ENTIRE child and
  multiplies with the child's own retries.
- Module top-level code runs on every folder scan — keep it side-effect free.
- Runs are capped at 10,000 step calls (runaway-loop guard).
- An Enum-typed input carries its `.value` in ctx, not the member.
- A dataclass with an unresolvable annotation surfaces as `inputs_error`
  on the flow and an empty form — keep annotations importable.

## Examples in workflows/

Flow.py (if/else + retry + dry-run) · Flow2.py (loop + branch + structured
logs) · Flow3.py (sub-workflows) · examples/HelloFlow (shared _lib +
log_image) · examples/OpsDashboard (widgets + inputs) ·
examples/ParallelFetch (parallel_map + backoff + webhook) ·
examples/RetryDemo (retry_on + continue_on_error) · examples/ResumeDemo
(resume, incl. inside a loop) · examples/LoopPatterns (tolerant loops).
